rationale: PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches the target trait (bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are bipolar I and bipolar II subtypes (partial matches). All three are otherwise near-clones (same publication, SDPR method, PGC training cohort, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, similar covariates, and no PRS-only AUC/R2), so the small differences in reported partial R² (0.00251 vs 0.00275/0.00307) are not strong enough to outweigh the clearer endpoint/label alignment advantage of PGS002786.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, same UKB portability publication, same training N (391,124), same covariates, same eval ancestry mix and validation N (19,864), and essentially identical partial-r performance (0.0563 vs 0.0562). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes to separate them, the main differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is generally favored for capturing polygenic signal when other evidence is tied. Therefore PGS002034 has the clearer multi-field advantage over the strongest runner-up (PGS001826).

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait/phenotyping (corneal dystrophy), same UKB portability publication, same training cohort/size (UKB; n=391,124), same covariates (age/sex/PCs etc.), and same evaluation ancestry mix/validation size. With endpoint fidelity and study context essentially identical and no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for either, the best differentiators are the comparable performance signal and structural properties. PGS002042 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) and is a genome-wide shrinkage score with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally favorable for capturing polygenic signal versus an extremely sparse penalized-regression model in this framework setting.

PGS002032 and PGS001824 are near-clone direct matches: same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Disorders of bilirubin excretion), same UKB portability study, same training N (391,124), same covariates, same multi-ancestry evaluation setup, and essentially identical partial-r (~0.0716) in the selected European validation record. In this near-clone setting, structural properties are the main differentiator: PGS002032 uses LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (19,768 variants) versus PGS001824’s much sparser penalized regression score (22 variants), which is less likely to capture polygenic signal robustly. PGS000924 reports very high PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it comes from a different pan-trait sparse UKB framework and has a less specific composite/time-to-event phenotype (porphyrin + bilirubin metabolism), making it a weaker direct-match choice despite cleaner metrics.

All candidates are near-clones: same endpoint (Major Depressive Disorder, lifetime; EFO major depressive disorder), same method (PRSice-2), same training cohort (UKB), same basic covariates (PCs 1-10), and same evaluation context/size. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes reported for any, the only differentiator visible is the selected validation R² (reported as variance explained) in the performance record; PGS003578 has the highest R² (0.0257), narrowly exceeding the strongest runner-up PGS003580 (0.0254). Given the otherwise identical metadata, that small but consistent metric edge makes PGS003578 the best-supported pick.

PGS001331 is the best direct-match: it targets Crohn’s disease with a straightforward diagnosis phenotype (phenotyping_reported: Crohns disease) and reports clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.579, PGS-only R²=0.00677) under basic covariates, with multi-ancestry evaluation present. The strongest runner-up is PGS001330, but it is a time-to-event (TTE) endpoint and has slightly weaker PRS-only performance (AUROC=0.576, R²=0.00621) with otherwise near-identical study family/covariates, so PGS001331 has the clearer endpoint fidelity and marginally better comparable metrics. PGS004254, despite a higher reported AUROC (0.72), only provides a full-model AUROC (no PRS-only AUC/R²) and comes from a different study context, making its performance less comparable for standalone PRS selection.

PGS005252 is the strongest direct match to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo both aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported incident aortic stenosis) and is also the top-ranked upstream pick. Versus the closest runner-up PGS005254 (also incident aortic stenosis, EUR), PGS005252 has a stronger reported per-SD effect size (HR 1.92 vs 1.64) and uses a similarly genome-wide shrinkage approach with comparable variant count (~1.12M). Although PGS005252 reports only a full-model C-index (0.87) with heavier clinical covariates (so not PRS-comparable), PGS005254 provides no PRS-only AUC/R2 either, leaving HR as the main comparable signal; on that basis PGS005252 has the clearer advantage. Other candidates (PGS005255/PGS005256) are valve-function measurement–labeled and the remaining models are for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, making them weaker endpoint matches.

PGS002755 is the strongest direct-match for atopic eczema/atopic dermatitis in this shortlist because it targets incident atopic dermatitis in a large European evaluation (n=337,910) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with very broad variant coverage (~1.09M), which is structurally better supported for a polygenic disease than the sparse GWAS-hit scores. The closest runner-up is PGS004587, which has the same incident AD endpoint and identical evaluation size/covariates, but is limited to 23 genome-wide significant SNPs and shows a weaker HR (1.153 vs 1.249 high-vs-low PRS), making it less likely to transfer as a strong standalone PRS. Other candidates are either endpoint-mismatched (paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis: PGS003486/PGS003459/PGS004903) or a different severity-defined phenotype with small validation and likely covariate-inflated full-model metrics (PGS001773).

PGS002738 is the best direct match to the target (trait_efo = alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported = Alcohol use disorder) and is supported by a disease-focused evaluation context (AUD PRS + family history paper) with a strong reported discrimination proxy (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). Compared with the strongest runner-up PGS002739, PGS002738 shows a higher top-decile OR (1.96 vs 1.76) and uses a genome-wide PRS (326k variants) rather than a very sparse gene-based score (858 variants), which is generally more appropriate for a polygenic disorder when no PRS-only AUC/R2 is available for any candidate. PGS000201/PGS000202 are less endpoint-faithful (problematic alcohol use / alcohol dependence measurement rather than AUD) and show smaller incremental R2 (0.0119 and 0.0046), making them weaker direct-match choices here.

PGS001263 is the only candidate with a direct atrial flutter endpoint across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, whereas the main alternatives (PGS001339/PGS002050/PGS001841) use the broader combined endpoint “atrial fibrillation and flutter” (and PGS001339 is additionally time-to-event). Between the two snpnet siblings from the same 813-traits UKB framework (PGS001263 vs PGS001339), PGS001263 also has slightly better PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.02517 vs 0.02447) with identical covariates and validation size/ancestry, and its PRS-only R2 remains below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0157; liability h2≈0.144). The portability-study scores (PGS002050/PGS001841) have larger training N and genome-wide methods but lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 here (only partial-r ~0.103), and their endpoint is not flutter-specific, so they do not show a clear multi-field advantage over the direct-match PGS001263.

All candidates are EUR-only and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we prioritize endpoint fidelity and within-family performance/effect-size signals. PGS000454 is a direct basal cell carcinoma endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all BCC) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs), and it has the strongest overall discrimination among the near-clone PRSweb siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 and the highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0489) with a strong per-SD OR 1.661. The closest runner-up PGS000452 is essentially identical in design and AUROC but has slightly weaker R² (0.0487) and weaker top-1% OR (3.61 vs 3.79). The 2023 MTAG-derived scores (PGS003416/PGS003417) have less endpoint fidelity because phenotyping_reported is broader ('Keratinocyte cancers') and they lack comparable performance metrics, so they are not promoted over the best-supported direct BCC PRSweb model.

All candidates are near-clones for the target (same PheCode 411.3 angina pectoris endpoint, same covariates age/sex/20 PCs, same MVP development cohort, same multi-ancestry GWAS/eval framing, same validation n=30,750; none report PRS-only AUC/R2 so full-model C-index is only a weak within-family tie-break). Given this like-for-like context, PGS005052 has the strongest effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.491, highest in the shortlist and closest to the ‘strong’ ~1.5 guideline) while maintaining essentially identical full-model C-index to the top runner-up PGS005048 (0.76625 vs 0.76688; difference is negligible). With no other clear multi-field advantage visible, the upstream top-ranked PGS005052 is the best-supported direct match.

PGS005313 is a direct atrial fibrillation match (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping all AF) from a disease-focused cross-population GWAS study and uses a cross-ancestry shrinkage approach (PRS-CSx) with very large genome-wide coverage (1,271,239 variants). It also reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.82, tight CI) and is evaluated in a multi-ancestry setting (selected validation ancestry spans European, African, South Asian, East Asian, Hispanic/LatAm, Other), which is supportive for external transfer. The strongest runner-up is PGS005168 (also AF, PRS-CS, multi-cohort), but its reported performance is a full-model C-index (0.8718) explicitly packaged with CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), which is strong negative evidence for standalone PRS comparability; its HR=1.67 is also slightly weaker than PGS005313’s OR signal. With no clean PRS-only AUC/R2 available for either, the cleaner covariate design plus cross-ancestry evaluation and strong effect size give PGS005313 the edge.

PGS004913 is the most endpoint-faithful, disease-focused direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis” and it was developed specifically for alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers, with clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a dedicated validation set (n=3,360, EUR). Versus the strongest runner-up PGS000704, although PGS000704 has far larger training/validation and a genome-wide model, it comes from a broad UKB framework-style paper and only reports a full-model C-index (0.711) with time-to-event covariates, which is not PRS-comparable and may be covariate-driven; its effect size is modest (HR 1.18). PGS001777 is a very sparse 3-variant score and its reported AUROC (0.671) is full-model with unknown covariates and a male-only phenotyping note, making it less clean and less general. Overall, PGS004913 best balances exact phenotype alignment with a disease-targeted study design and interpretable PRS signal (R2=0.029; OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4) without obvious clinical-risk packaging.

PGS005134 is the strongest direct-match asthma PRS in this shortlist because it comes from a disease-focused, asthma-specific multi-ancestry meta-analysis study family (Cell Genomics 2025) using a cross-ancestry shrinkage method (PRS-CSx) and reports a PRS-relevant variance explained (R²=0.0536) under basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). This edges out the strongest runner-up PGS001344, which has clean PGS-only AUROC/R² but is from the known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“813 traits” snpnet) that domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external transfer despite tidy metrics. Compared with other framework/portability candidates (PGS002061/PGS001849) that only report partial-r and with PGS002727 which is pediatric-specific and reports only full-model AUROC, PGS005134 offers the best combination of endpoint fidelity, study archetype, and PRS signal consistent with the asthma heritability ceiling.

PGS003428 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused cervical cancer PRS in the shortlist: it is derived from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis study (not a pan-trait framework), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (~2.9M), and reports a moderate PRS effect size (HR per SD 1.33) with only light covariate adjustment (age, smoking). The main runner-up is PGS000073/PGS000784, but those are 10-SNP genome-wide-significant hit scores from cross-cancer risk-factor integration papers with much heavier covariate packaging (parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years, etc.), and their higher full-model AUROC (~0.745) is not PRS-comparable and likely covariate-driven; their PRS signal (HR ~1.21–1.22) is weaker than PGS003428’s. PGS001299 has clean PGS-only metrics but is a sparse pan-trait UKB framework score with very low PRS-only AUROC (~0.55) and R2 (~0.0026), making it less likely to benchmark well than the disease-focused LDpred model.

All candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO, but PGS000753 has the cleanest disease-focused endpoint specification ("Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm") and provides the most directly PRS-informative evidence via an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, moderate signal) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). The strongest runner-up is PGS003973/PGS003972 (same Nat Genet AAA meta-analysis, genome-wide PRS-CS), but their reported discrimination is only full-model (C-index/AUROC) and thus not PRS-comparable; the very high 0.882 in PGS003973 is likely covariate-driven (age/sex) and cannot be used as a standalone PRS quality advantage. Framework/portability scores (PGS002054, PGS001784) are penalized as pan-trait outputs despite having PRS-only R2/partial-r, and PGS003429 appears tied to screening cost-effectiveness packaging with only full-model metrics and unknown covariates. Given the lack of PRS-only AUC/R2 for the disease-focused Nat Genet scores, PGS000753’s coherent disease-focused design plus explicit OR makes it the best-supported pick.

PGS002034 and PGS001826 are near-clone direct matches to a specific coagulation disorder subtype (congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency / factor VII deficiency) from the same UKB portability study with the same covariates and essentially identical partial-r (~0.0563 vs 0.0562). In this near-tie, PGS002034 has a clear structural advantage (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants), which is the most meaningful differentiator given the otherwise indistinguishable endpoint and evaluation context. PGS001033 has an exact EFO match to the broad target (‘blood coagulation disease’) and reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it comes from the pan-trait sparse UKB framework (‘813 traits’) with an extremely sparse 1-variant model and a time-to-event phenotype, which is a weaker and less reliable archetype for external performance than the better-structured genome-wide score among the direct-match siblings.

All candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy and are from disease-focused Nat Genet studies using PRS-CS, so endpoint fidelity is broadly acceptable. Compared with the strongest runner-up (PGS004862), PGS004949 provides explicit PRS-only discrimination (univariate PRS-only AUC=0.68 with CI) and PRS contribution metrics (delta R²), whereas PGS004862 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (not PRS-comparable). Within the 2024-12-16 sibling set, PGS004949 has the highest PRS-only AUC (0.68 vs 0.67/0.66/0.65/0.64) with strong per-SD OR (~1.91), making it the best-supported candidate on comparable PRS performance evidence while remaining phenotype-aligned (non-ischemic DCM is still a direct DCM endpoint).

PGS002237 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused CKD score in the shortlist: it targets CKD stage ≥3 with a clearly specified clinical phenotype (eGFR <45) and is explicitly designed to predict CKD across ancestries, with multi-ancestry evaluation reported (AFR/AMR/ASN/EUR/MAE) and a large UKB development sample (n=279,819). Its reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.47) is the strongest among the candidates shown, supporting meaningful PRS signal even though only full-model AUROC is provided. The closest runner-up is PGS005090, which shows a very high AUROC (0.90) but this is full-model (not PRS-only) and is likely covariate-inflated; it also has narrower transportability (AFR-only GWAS/EVAL) and lacks training sample details. The remaining candidates (PGS004158/PGS004030/PGS004045/PGS004142) are benchmarking-family scores with much weaker discrimination (AUROC ~0.586–0.592) and smaller training (n=13,496), making them less likely to top an external benchmark for generic CKD risk.

PGS001268 and PGS001267 are the strongest direct-match candidates because they report clean PRS-only (no-covariates) AUROC/R² on a large European validation (n=67,425) with only basic covariates, and their PRS-only R² (~0.10) is plausible relative to the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability~0.40). Between these near-clone siblings from the same study (same method, variants, cohorts, ancestry context), PGS001268 has consistently slightly better PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.7346 vs 0.7265; R² 0.1023 vs 0.0988), making it the best-supported pick. The higher-ranked PGS002089 is from a portability framework and lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R² (only partial-r=0.0919), so it does not have a clear multi-field advantage over the snpnet scores; the Taiwanese EAS-only models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation (n=1,298), making them less reliable for general benchmarking.

PGS004546 is the top-ranked candidate and is an exact endpoint match to the target (ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis in both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported, trait_efo=cholelithiasis) with large genome-wide coverage (1,059,939 variants) and a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.30). Its strongest runner-up is the near-clone sibling PGS004476 from the same study, same endpoint, same ancestry context, and same variant count; PGS004546 has the stronger reported effect size (OR 1.30 vs 1.22), which is a legitimate within-family tie-break when other fields are essentially identical. Other alternatives are either framework/portability scores with weaker endpoint fidelity (cholelithiasis+cholecystitis) and non-AUC metrics (partial-r), or a pan-trait sparse UKB score (PGS001174) with modest PRS-only AUROC/R2 and a time-to-event endpoint, which domain guidance suggests should not automatically outrank a coherent disease-focused exact-endpoint model family.

PGS001135 is the only candidate that directly matches the broad target trait (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=Arthritis (nos)) and also provides clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R2=0.00291), which are sanity-consistent with the provided low heritability ceiling. The strongest runner-up is PGS004547 (same EFO and a more specific ICD10-style endpoint “Other arthritis” with a meta/ensemble method), but it lacks any PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and only reports a modest OR (1.26), making its standalone PRS strength less supported from the visible evidence; PGS004477 is similar but with an even weaker OR (~1.20). The remaining candidates are juvenile idiopathic arthritis subtypes (different EFO/endpoint), so they are poorer direct matches for generic ‘arthritis’ despite higher reported full-model AUROCs.

PGS001783 and PGS001788 are the strongest direct COPD matches (same trait_reported/efo/phenotyping, same publication family, same method PRS-CS-auto, similar multi-biobank training context, and basic covariates without clinical leakage). Between these near-clones, PGS001783 has a clear PRS-comparable performance advantage: higher covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only R2 (0.038092 vs 0.0163), and this remains below the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0122; h2_liab≈0.0388), making it plausible and informative. The snpnet UKB framework scores (PGS001332/333/334) have much weaker PRS-only R2 (~0.002–0.003) and are from a pan-trait sparse framework; the UKB portability scores (PGS002062/PGS001850) use a less specific ‘chronic airway obstruction’ endpoint and report only partial-r, with weaker estimates than PGS001783’s PRS-only R2. Although PGS001788 has a much larger validation N, validation size is a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the materially stronger PRS-only R2 of PGS001783.

PGS000316 is the best-supported direct match because it is a disease-focused coeliac disease score intended for clinical diagnostic aid (phenotyping_reported and trait_reported both coeliac disease) and is evaluated at very large scale (validation n=379,767) with strong reported discrimination (AUROC 0.879, albeit as a full-model metric). The main runner-up is PGS001301, which uniquely reports clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.8287; PGS-only R2 0.1422), but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“across 813 traits”) with a broader/less specific endpoint label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which domain guidance flags as typically less reliable for external performance than a disease-focused model when endpoint fidelity is available. Other candidates either report only full-model AUROC on much smaller validations (PGS000040) or are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (PGS000041/PGS000042), or are portability-framework scores with weaker partial-r metrics (PGS002067/PGS001856).

PGS005170 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused dementia PRS in the shortlist: it targets incident all-cause dementia (trait_efo=dementia; phenotyping_reported=Incident all-cause dementia) and uses an integrative ensemble of 24 component PRSs with very large genome-wide coverage (1,320,229 variants) and explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR), which is supportive for external transfer. The main runner-up on PRS-comparable metrics is PGS000946 (UKB pan-trait snpnet), which reports clean PGS-only AUROC/R2 (0.641/0.025) but comes from the known '813 traits in UK Biobank' framework archetype with very sparse variant sets (9 variants) and an internally optimized single-biobank setting that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external validation. PGS005170’s reported AUROC is full-model (0.761) and includes APOE allele dosage as a covariate (so not PRS-only comparable), lowering confidence, but its endpoint fidelity + disease-focused integrative construction and broader evaluation context provide a clearer multi-field advantage over the framework scores.

PGS004621 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported = Cirrhosis) and is built as a genome-wide PRS (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants), which is structurally better suited to capture polygenic signal than the sparse GWAS-hit scores in the shortlist. It also comes from a clearly disease-focused, multi-cohort cirrhosis genetics study (Nat Genet; multiple biobanks listed) with very large European evaluation (n=1,153,995) and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), reducing concerns about clinical-risk packaging. The strongest runner-up is PGS000726 (also cirrhosis of liver), but it is a 12-variant genome-wide-significant score with no comparable PRS-only AUC/R2 and offers less polygenic coverage; the remaining candidates are alcohol-specific cirrhosis endpoints (trait_efo alcoholic liver cirrhosis) or time-to-event/at-risk subgroup phenotyping, making them less faithful to generic cirrhosis of liver.

All candidates are direct matches for breast carcinoma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align) and come from the same publication family with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (12,483), covariates reported as 0, and the same evaluation context (EUR with some SAS; same validation N=48,968). With no PRS-only AUC/R² available for any candidate, the best differentiators are within-family performance/effect-size signals and structural advantages. PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the highest reported AUROC (0.6625 vs 0.6598 for the closest runner-up PGS004040) and the strongest effect size (OR per SD 1.826 vs 1.809), and it also benefits from an ensemble/multi-score aggregation method, which is a positive structural signal when endpoints and covariates are otherwise identical. The AUROC differences are small, but combined with consistently higher OR and the ensemble structure, PGS004153 has the clearest multi-field edge over PGS004040.

PGS000327 is the cleaner direct match on endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder,” whereas PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn),” a clear endpoint mismatch despite the ASD label. PGS000327 also has stronger and more interpretable disease-focused evidence (multi-cohort ASD GWAS context; reports an OR=1.33 per SD and R²=0.0245) versus PGS002790’s weaker partial R² (~0.0055) from a broader sex-specific psychiatric/cognition study framing. Both are EUR-only and neither provides PRS-only AUC/R², so the decisive advantage is PGS000327’s coherent ASD diagnosis endpoint plus stronger effect-size/variance-explained signal.

All candidates are direct CAD matches, but PGS003725 is the top-ranked member of a coherent, disease-focused Nat Med 2023 multi-ancestry CAD PRS family using the same LDpred2 pipeline and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) with broad multi-ancestry evaluation. Versus the strongest runner-up within the same family (PGS003726), PGS003725 shows slightly stronger reported effect sizes (HR 1.75 vs 1.73; also reports OR 2.14) with otherwise similar validation size and endpoint framing, making it the best-supported pick. Older alternatives (e.g., PGS000013/PGS002244) are also CAD but either provide weaker effect-size evidence here (OR 1.64 for PGS002244) or are older portability-style scores; PGS000013’s PRS-only R2=0.04 is informative but does not clearly outweigh the newer multi-ancestry disease-focused score’s stronger per-SD risk gradients and broader evaluation context.

PGS004944 is the top-ranked candidate and has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (primary open-angle glaucoma; EFO open-angle glaucoma) with very large validation (n=407,667) and supportive PRS effect size evidence (OR per SD 1.74). Although it reports only a full-model AUROC (0.748) rather than PRS-only metrics, its covariates are relatively basic (age/sex/ancestry), avoiding the explicit family-history packaging seen in PGS000137. The strongest runner-up is PGS001792, which provides a clean PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out = 0.03209) and similar POAG endpoint, but it comes from a global biobank framework paper and lacks effect-size support; its PRS-only R2 advantage is modest and not a clear multi-field win over PGS004944’s larger validation and stronger OR evidence.

All three candidates are direct phenotype matches for Dupuytren contracture, but PGS002092 and PGS001880 are near-clone siblings from the same UKB portability study with identical training cohort (UKB), training N (391,124), covariates, and multi-ancestry evaluation context. In that near-clone setting, the best available comparable performance signal is the selected European partial correlation, where PGS002092 is slightly higher than PGS001880 (partial-r 0.0797 vs 0.0783) and it also uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (LDpred2, 484,484 vs 2,443), a structural advantage for polygenic signal capture. PGS001254 reports clean PRS-only AUROC/R2, but it comes from the sparse pan-trait UKB framework paper (813 traits) with only 11 variants, which is a known weaker archetype for external transfer compared with the better-structured genome-wide portability scores here; its metric edge is not enough to outweigh that structural/framework disadvantage against the strongest sibling pair.

PGS002304 has the cleanest endpoint fidelity for the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to follicular lymphoma), whereas the main alternative with the same trait_reported (PGS003455) has an explicit phenotyping mismatch (phenotyping_reported = chronic lymphocytic leukemia), making it endpoint-incoherent despite sharing the EFO. Compared with the PRSweb candidates (PGS000644/PGS000643), which are labeled/phenotyped as “nodular lymphoma” (only mapped via EFO) and come from a pan-cancer repository framework, PGS002304 is supported by a disease-focused multi-cohort cancer evaluation context and shows higher reported discrimination in its selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.61 vs ~0.53 for PGS000644/PGS000643), with no evidence of heavy covariate packaging in the metadata (covariates unknown rather than explicitly augmented). All candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so endpoint coherence and study archetype drive the choice.

All three candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_efo=Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported=lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same multi-cohort, multi-ancestry study family with identical validation size (n=94,651) and unknown covariates, and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC). In this setting, effect-size strength and structural method signals are the most informative differentiators: PGS005271 (PRSCS, genome-wide) shows the strongest per-SD effect (OR=1.55; β=0.44), indicating materially stronger PRS signal than the main runner-up PGS005270 (P+T, OR=1.037; β=0.037) despite PGS005270’s slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.630), which is not a reliable PRS-only comparator. PGS005272 has weaker full-model AUROC (0.605) and lower OR (1.42) than PGS005271, so PGS005271 is best-supported overall.

All candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (CHF PheCode 428.1; EFO congestive heart failure), covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), training cohort (MVP), ancestry context, and validation size (n=31,804), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—only full-model C-index plus per-SD OR. In this same-study, same-endpoint cluster, the best-supported tie-break is the strongest within-context performance/effect size: PGS005083 has the highest reported full-model C-index (0.75368) and the highest OR per SD (1.455) versus the closest runner-up PGS005077 (C-index 0.75358; OR 1.452). The differences are small, so confidence is moderate, but PGS005083 has the clearest multi-field edge within an otherwise indistinguishable set.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical trait/phenotyping (“Disorders of iron metabolism”), identical covariates (basic demographics + PCs), identical training size and evaluation ancestry mix, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2. With endpoint fidelity and study context effectively tied, the best differentiators are the within-family performance and structural signals: PGS002031 shows slightly higher partial correlation (0.1355 vs 0.1307) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with many more variants (6713 vs 654), which is generally favorable for capturing polygenic signal compared with a much sparser penalized regression score in this framework setting. Therefore PGS002031 is the better-supported direct match over PGS001823.

PGS000054 is the best direct-match because it has clean endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo both late-onset Alzheimer’s disease; phenotyping_reported is familial late-onset AD) and, crucially, it provides the strongest PRS-discrimination signal available in this shortlist via an OR per SD of 1.73 (vs 1.29 for its near-clone sibling PGS000053). Both PGS000054 and PGS000053 come from the same Neurology study, use the same GWAS-hits construction (21 variants) and the same basic covariates (age, sex), so the materially stronger effect size in PGS000054 is a legitimate tie-break. The main runner-up is PGS000053 (same study/endpoint/covariates but weaker OR). PGS000334 and PGS004918 only report full-model R²/AUROC with unknown covariates (not PRS-comparable), and PGS002289’s phenotyping is cognition/age-interaction rather than AD case-control, making it a weaker endpoint match despite huge validation N.

PGS002763 is the cleanest direct match to the target (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Hip osteoarthritis”, EFO matches) and is built as a genome-wide shrinkage PRS (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), avoiding proxy endpoints and risk-wrapper packaging. It also reports a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46), consistent with meaningful PRS signal. The strongest runner-up is PGS004882, which has a very large evaluation sample and an HR=1.4, but it is an incident/time-to-event, country-incidence framework-style score with only a full-model C-index reported (0.60) and an implausibly tiny training N shown (n=404), making its PRS evidence less directly comparable and less clearly supported than PGS002763’s straightforward disease-endpoint PRS.

All candidates are for hypothyroidism, but several are pan-trait/framework-style (PGS000965, PGS001181 from the “813 traits” UKB sparse snpnet paper) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation despite clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 reporting. The top-ranked PGS005218 is disease-focused and very large, but its only reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC (0.859) with heavy near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), making that metric non-comparable for standalone PRS ranking and likely covariate-driven. PGS002766 provides a direct hypothyroidism endpoint with basic covariates and a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.43–1.52), which is a more reliable PRS-quality signal than covariate-inflated full-model AUROC; it also avoids the framework penalty affecting PGS000965/PGS001181 and has stronger validation support than the portability-style PGS004935 (small eval n=8,417, unknown covariates).

PGS004911 is the strongest direct-match: it targets hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (“Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~374k), and is evaluated in a large EUR sample (n=343,182) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), minimizing clinical leakage. Versus its near-clone sibling PGS004910 (same study, endpoint, covariates, ancestry, and validation size), PGS004911 shows consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence (higher full-model AUROC 0.80 vs 0.73; higher HR 2.34 vs 1.97; higher OR per SD 1.33 vs 1.26; slightly higher high-vs-median tertile OR 5.9 vs 5.5), making it the better-supported pick within the same context. Older alternatives are weaker: PGS000739 uses only 27 GWAS-significant variants and includes heavy clinical covariates (risk factors + rare variant carrier status), making its AUROC less comparable to a standalone PRS; PGS000778 has a mismatched specialized endpoint (events among pathogenic sarcomeric variant carriers) and tiny validation (n=368).

PGS000639 is the strongest direct-match Hodgkin’s lymphoma candidate in the shortlist: it has coherent endpoint alignment across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (all Hodgkin’s disease/lymphoma) and, within the same Cancer PRSweb sibling set (PGS000638/PGS000637/PGS000640) with identical ancestry (EUR), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), training (MGI; n=736) and validation size (n=775), it shows the best reported discrimination/effect evidence (highest full-model AUROC 0.62 and strongest per-SD OR 1.476). The main runner-up is PGS000638 (same design) but it is consistently weaker on AUROC (0.601) and OR (1.377). PGS003449 is penalized by clear phenotype incoherence (phenotyping_reported is chronic lymphocytic leukemia despite Hodgkin lymphoma label) and very weak effect size (OR ~1.02), while PGS000080/PGS000791 are for non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma (wrong trait).

PGS004908 is the strongest direct-match overall: it targets kidney cancer/renal carcinoma with coherent phenotyping (“Kidney cancer”), comes from a large, disease-focused multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; BBJ/FinnGen/NCI), and—critically—shows the strongest PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58) with a substantially larger variant set (107) than the older GWAS-hits kidney cancer scores. The main runner-up is PGS000076 (and its near-clone PGS000787), which has similar endpoint framing (incident kidney cancer; RCC EFO) and large evaluation, but its PRS effect size is notably weaker (HR ~1.16 per SD) and it is an older cross-cancer evaluation built on only 19 variants. Although all candidates lack clean PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is not decisive), the combination of stronger per-SD effect size and more recent, disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS support makes PGS004908 the best-supported choice.

PGS000114 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all directly match the target umbrella endpoint (juvenile idiopathic arthritis), whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are subtype-specific JIA scores (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular) and thus are less faithful to the generic target trait. All candidates come from the same disease-focused publication, use the same method (SparSNP), have the same basic covariates (sex, PCs 1–10), and are EUR-only in development/evaluation, so endpoint fidelity is the main differentiator. Although PGS000324 shows a much higher reported full-model AUROC (0.93) and OR (3.09), these are not PRS-only metrics and are for a narrower subtype endpoint, so they are not a clear advantage for the broad JIA target over the exact umbrella JIA model.

PGS004614 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused diverticular disease score in the shortlist: it targets the exact trait (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Diverticular disease”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR) with very large variant coverage (~1.08M), and comes from a dedicated diverticular disease GWAS paper. The main runner-up is the Commun Biol pair (PGS004544/PGS004474), which are also ICD10 K57-aligned but are framed as “risk factor PRS + disease PRS” integration (packaging risk) and provide only modest per-SD ORs (~1.31–1.32) with unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2. The older snpnet framework scores (PGS000997/PGS000996) do report PRS-only AUC/R2, but they are from a pan-trait UKB workflow and show weak PRS-only discrimination (AUC ~0.59 / 0.55; R2 ~0.018 / 0.004), making them less likely to outperform a newer disease-focused genome-wide score in external benchmarks. PGS004614’s reported AUROC (0.76) is full-model and includes family history (so not PRS-comparable), which lowers confidence, but overall endpoint fidelity + disease-focused study archetype + method/coverage advantage still favor it over the alternatives.

PGS004236 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused hypertension score in the shortlist: it targets hypertension with a clear prevalent-hypertension endpoint, is developed/validated in a multi-cohort, multi-ancestry setting (BioMe/MVP/UKB; diverse evaluation ancestries), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.1) supporting meaningful PRS signal even though only full-model AUROC is shown. The closest runner-up is its same-paper sibling PGS004234, which has essentially identical endpoint/covariates/validation but weaker supporting evidence (no effect size reported and slightly lower full-model AUROC), so PGS004236 has the clearer empirical edge within that near-clone family. Other candidates are penalized as pan-trait/framework-style (PGS001320) or have weaker/less-informative evidence packages (PGS004934/PGS002998: only full-model AUROC with smaller/less robust validation context; PGS000957/PGS000958: essential-hypertension/time-to-event variants rather than the generic hypertension target).

PGS004562 is the strongest direct match to the target kidney failure in this shortlist because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="kidney failure" with an ICD-anchored endpoint (N18 chronic renal failure) and comes from a disease-prediction study that uses a multi-score aggregation approach (RFDiseasemetaPRS), which is a positive structural signal versus single-score methods. Against its closest runner-up PGS004492 (same publication, same endpoint, same ancestry and sample sizes), PGS004562 shows materially stronger per-SD effect size evidence (OR 1.395 vs 1.171), making it the better-supported sibling within an otherwise near-clone pair. Other candidates are less endpoint-faithful to kidney failure (CKD stage 3+, CKD/dialysis) or are framework-style/weak PRS-signal (PGS001272 PGS-only AUROC 0.536, R2 0.002) or have subtype mismatch (PGS000708 diabetic kidney failure).

For the target trait hyperthyroidism, the Graves’ disease models are acceptable direct matches (Graves’ is a clinically dominant cause of hyperthyroidism) and come from a disease-focused, multi-biobank study with large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=94,651 across African American/Hispanic/European). Among the three near-clone Graves’ candidates from the same publication family (PGS005265/PGS005266/PGS005264), PGS005265 has the strongest available discriminative evidence (highest reported AUROC 0.6652 and strongest per-SD effect size OR=1.63 vs 1.54 for PGS005266; PGS005264 is clearly weaker with near-null OR≈1.01). The main runner-up is PGS001042 (exact thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism label with clean PGS-only AUC/R2), but it is a pan-trait UKB framework score and its PRS-only R2 (~0.024) is modest; given domain guidance that disease-focused multi-cohort scores typically transfer better than UKB framework scores when endpoint alignment is acceptable, PGS005265 is the better-supported choice despite lacking explicit PGS-only metrics.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; EFO Nasal Cavity Polyp), publication/study family, ancestry (EUR dev/eval), training cohort (UKB), training N (174,489) and validation N (56,192), and neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 or covariates. With metrics absent, the main differentiator is available effect-size evidence and model structure: PGS004535 reports a materially stronger per-SD OR (1.60) than PGS004465 (1.35), and it is an explicit meta/ensemble-style construction (RFDiseasemetaPRS) versus a single-score LDpred2, which is a positive structural signal when otherwise comparable. Therefore PGS004535 is the better-supported direct-match choice.

Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical endpoint framing (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder; trait_efo: nicotine dependence), similar basic covariates, same training cohort/size, and same validation sample size, so performance evidence is the main differentiator. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS002037 shows a higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557 for PGS001830) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (LDpred2, 847,691 vs penalized regression, 13,838), which is a supportive structural advantage for a polygenic trait in the absence of cleaner PRS-only metrics.

PGS004606 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused AMD PRS in the shortlist: it targets age-related macular degeneration with a clear clinical endpoint (phenotyping_reported matches), uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and shows strong PRS signal via OR per SD=1.76 with a large European validation (n=163,011) under only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). The main runner-up is its near-clone sibling PGS004607 from the same Nat Genet study, but it is disadvantaged by training on AFR-only GWAS while still evaluated in EUR and has materially weaker reported performance (full-model AUROC 0.65 vs 0.71; OR 1.48 vs 1.76). Other candidates are either framework/portability UKB scores with weak effect metrics (PGS001834/PGS002041), a broad self-reported UKB framework score with low PRS-only AUC/R2 (PGS001013), or a small GWAS-hits score with very small validation and a subtype endpoint (PGS004952).

All candidates are direct matches for gout (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align), come from the same publication family, have identical training cohort (UKB), training N (6,704), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), validation size (90,274), and covariates listed as 0—so the main differentiators are within-family performance and structural method signals. PGS004160 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest reported discrimination in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.6936; R² 0.0893) and the strongest effect size (OR per SD 2.05) versus the closest runner-up PGS004047 (AUROC 0.6851; R² 0.0801; OR 2.00). Given the near-clone context and absence of PRS-only AUC/R² for all models, the combination of (i) multi-score ensemble method and (ii) consistently best AUROC/R²/OR within the same endpoint/covariate setting makes PGS004160 the best-supported pick.

All candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (MI PheCode 411.2; trait_efo myocardial infarction), covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), cohorts (MVP), ancestry distribution, and validation size (n=30,379), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so full-model C-index differences are only a weak tie-break. Within this same-study sibling set, PGS005039 has the strongest available empirical signals: the highest reported full-model C-index (0.7848 vs ~0.7831–0.7839 for others) and the largest per-SD OR (1.578 vs 1.527–1.554), edging out the closest runner-up PGS005045 (C-index 0.7839; OR 1.554). Given the otherwise indistinguishable metadata, this consistent (though small) advantage makes PGS005039 the best-supported direct-match choice.

PGS002767 is the strongest direct match on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly “Knee osteoarthritis”) with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.05M variants) and clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), avoiding risk-factor packaging. It also shows a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.30–1.40) in a reasonably sized EUR validation (n=39,444). The closest runner-up is PGS002729, which is disease-focused and multi-cohort but uses only 24 GWAS-significant variants and reports only a full-model AUROC (0.66) with added BMI (not PRS-comparable), plus its phenotyping is broader (“Clinical osteoarthritis”) rather than knee-specific. Framework-style PGS001192 has clean PRS-only metrics but comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse-score paper and shows weak PRS-only performance (AUROC~0.557; R2=0.0068), making it less likely to benchmark well than a knee-OA-focused genome-wide score.

PGS002082 is the best direct match to the target trait at the EFO level (lupus erythematosus) and has coherent endpoint wording (“Lupus (localized and systemic)”) without subtype restriction, plus a method/structure advantage over the closest sibling PGS001870: LDpred2 with a genome-wide variant set (361,553 vs 87 variants) and a higher PRS-comparable signal in the same portability study context (partial-r 0.0212 vs 0.0184, same UKB training, same covariates, same multi-ancestry evaluation design). Competing SLE-specific candidates (e.g., PGS000754/PGS000328/PGS000196/PGS003960/PGS004917) either rely only on full-model AUROC (not PRS-only comparable here) and/or have endpoint/covariate issues (notably PGS003960 uses a phenotype risk score covariate, and PGS000328 is early-onset only), so they do not present a clear multi-field advantage over the top-ranked, endpoint-aligned PGS002082.

All candidates are nominally mapped to multiple myeloma, but PGS003450 has an explicit endpoint mismatch (phenotyping_reported = Chronic lymphocytic leukemia), making it a weaker direct match despite large n. Among the remaining direct-match scores, none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative; however PGS002281 is a disease-focused multiple-myeloma PRS paper with clean/basic covariates (age, sex, region) and substantially larger validation (n=2,395) than the closest runner-up PGS002306 (also GW-significant 23 variants but n=290 and covariates unknown). The older PRSweb scores (PGS000652/653/654) show materially lower full-model AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and similar sparse architectures, so they are less supported here. Therefore PGS002281 is the best-supported direct-match candidate.

PGS000077 is the best direct match to the target trait (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia; phenotyping_reported=Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia) and is the canonical, correctly oriented score (75 genome-wide significant variants) from the cross-cancer evaluation study. The strongest runner-up is PGS000788, which uses the same 75 variants but explicitly applies inverse variant weights (a packaging/orientation red flag) and comes from a PRS+modifiable-risk-factor integration paper where the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (not PRS-only) and thus not a clean advantage. The other candidates (PGS000645 and PGS000646–PGS000649) are mostly chronic lymphocytic leukemia (different EFO) and/or much smaller, single-biobank PRSweb evaluations with weaker discrimination (full-model AUROC ~0.67–0.70 for CLL; 0.578 for lymphoid leukemia with only 6 variants), making them less faithful to the broad lymphoid leukemia target and less supported for general benchmarking.

PGS005235 is the strongest direct-match obesity candidate on endpoint fidelity and PRS-strength signals: although labeled broadly as “Adiposity,” its phenotyping is explicitly an obesity diagnosis (phecode 278.1) with basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs) and it reports a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97) than the closest runner-up cluster PGS004447/PGS004517 (E66 obesity but weaker OR≈1.36/1.23 and unknown covariates). Compared with the UKB framework/portability scores (PGS002033/PGS001825) and the pan-trait sparse TTE model (PGS001298), PGS005235 is more disease-endpoint anchored (diagnosis phecode rather than broad “hyperalimentation” bundle or time-to-event packaging) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with substantial variant coverage, making it more likely to transfer well in external benchmarks.

All candidates map to the same disease concept, but PGS000809 is the most disease-focused, consortium-style MS score (many MS GWAS cohorts listed, IMSGC included) with clean/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a reasonable variant set (127) typical of established MS risk loci. The strongest runner-up is PGS002726 (Brain), which shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.80) and a strong top-decile OR (15), but it has much smaller validation (n=938) and unknown covariates, and its extremely large variant count paired with a 'genome-wide significant variants' label is internally inconsistent, reducing trust in the metadata/performance comparability. The UKB framework/portability scores (PGS001270/PGS001271/PGS002038/PGS001831) provide cleaner PRS-only/partial-r metrics but come from pan-trait/portability archetypes that typically underperform disease-focused consortium scores in external benchmarks when a direct disease model exists. PGS004699 is heavily context-packaged around optic neuritis presentation rather than generic MS risk, despite huge evaluation N, so it is less direct for the target trait.

PGS005262 is the best direct match to the target “nodular goiter” because its endpoint is explicitly benign nodular goiter (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align), whereas PGS001814/PGS002022 target nontoxic multinodular goiter (related but not the same label) and PGS005273/PGS005274 are case-control contrasts (thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter) rather than nodular goiter risk. Within the strongest same-study, same-endpoint sibling set (PGS005262 vs PGS005263 vs PGS005261), PGS005262 has the strongest available empirical signals: highest reported AUROC in the selected record (0.5933 vs 0.5876 vs 0.5854) and the largest per-SD effect size (OR 1.41 vs 1.36 vs 1.05), with similar multi-cohort, multi-ancestry evaluation context and no cleaner PRS-only metrics available to overturn this ordering.

All candidates are melanoma direct matches in EUR and none reports a clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative and covariate packaging matters. PGS000813 has the strongest disease-focused evidence package among the top-ranked options: it reports the highest full-model AUROC (0.77, 95% CI 0.75–0.79) with only basic covariates (age, sex) and provides strong PRS effect-size evidence (OR per SD 2.12; top 10% vs middle 20% OR 5.7), suggesting substantial standalone PRS signal. The strongest runner-up, PGS000743, has a lower AUROC (0.74) but uses extensive traditional risk factors including family history and other non-genetic predictors, making its AUROC less attributable to the PRS and less comparable. The Br J Dermatol evaluation-family scores (PGS002247/PGS002246/PGS002253) have cleaner covariates (age, sex) and incident invasive melanoma endpoints, but show materially lower AUROC (~0.69/0.66) and no effect-size advantage in the visible fields. Therefore PGS000813 is the best-supported direct-match candidate here.

PGS000083 is the best-supported direct match: it targets pancreatic cancer (EFO exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) with an incident endpoint and is evaluated at very large scale in Europeans (n=391,491) with consistent effect size evidence (HR=1.49 per SD) in a cross-cancer evaluation setting. The strongest runner-up is PGS000794, but it is explicitly the same 22-variant score with inverse weights and shows essentially identical full-model AUROC/C-index and HR, offering no clear multi-field advantage over the upstream-picked PGS000083. Other candidates either have much smaller validation (PGS000663), weaker reported discrimination (PGS000725/PGS000385), unclear/packaged clinical-risk covariates and unspecified evaluation ancestry despite high full-model AUROC (PGS002264), or sparse/limited metric support (PGS004250).

Both candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis (trait_efo=otosclerosis), but PGS001255 provides cleaner, PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.6319 and PGS-only R2=0.01341 (with basic covariates only in the full model), and the PRS-only R2 is plausible relative to the provided h2_obs ceiling (~0.0048) given scale differences and remains small (not an obvious inflation). The main runner-up PGS002046 is from a portability framework and, while it uses a stronger genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many more variants and larger training N, it lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and only reports partial-r=0.0182, giving weaker direct evidence of standalone PRS discrimination for this endpoint. With endpoint fidelity otherwise similar and no heavy covariate leakage in either, the presence of explicit PRS-only metrics tips the balance to PGS001255 despite its framework-paper origin.

PGS000082 is the best direct match to the broad target “ovarian neoplasm” because it targets incident ovarian cancer (ovarian carcinoma EFO) in a large European evaluation (n=211,958) and represents the original disease-focused cross-cancer evaluation score. The strongest runner-up is PGS000793, but it is explicitly a re-weighted/inverted version of PGS000082 with essentially the same endpoint and covariate package; its slightly higher full-model AUROC/R² are not PRS-only metrics and are not a clear advantage given the near-clone relationship and potential comparability issues. Other candidates either shift to narrower subtypes (serous carcinoma; non-mucinous epithelial) or to horizon/BRCA2-carrier-specific risk packaging, reducing fidelity to the generic ovarian neoplasm target.

PGS003586 is the strongest direct match for the target trait preeclampsia: it is explicitly labeled Pre-eclampsia with trait_efo=preeclampsia and uses a disease-focused multi-cohort Nat Med study design with only basic covariates (maternal age, age^2, PCs). Versus the closest runner-up PGS003587 (same paper, same method, same evaluation ancestry and validation size), PGS003586 has better endpoint fidelity (gestational hypertension label is a partial mismatch) and a materially stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.31 vs 1.20), which is the main differentiator given both lack PRS-only AUC/R2. PGS004593 has weaker phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported=Gestational hypertension despite trait_reported=Preeclampsia) and a weaker effect size signal (HR 1.16), so its larger validation N does not outweigh the endpoint/performance disadvantages.

Both candidates map cleanly to the target (trait_efo = psoriatic arthritis), but PGS001287 has substantially stronger PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.676) and PGS-only R² (0.0335) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), and these values are plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability ~0.0735). It is also evaluated in a large European validation sample (n=24,905) with additional multi-ancestry evaluation records. In contrast, PGS000342 provides only a full-model AUROC (0.562) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics, plus a much smaller validation (n=543), making its PRS strength and comparability less supported despite the exact trait label.

PGS000078 is the best-supported direct match because it targets incident lung cancer (trait_reported/trait_efo aligned) and is evaluated at very large scale in Europeans (n=392,539), with consistent time-to-event discrimination reported (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849) and an HR per SD ~1.16. The strongest runner-up is PGS004860, which uses a genome-wide LDpred2 score (structurally attractive) and reports higher full-model AUROC (0.893) and OR 1.33, but it is supported by only a single, much smaller French-Canadian case-control cohort (n=24,012) and its reported AUROC is likewise full-model and not PRS-only, making the apparent performance edge less reliable for benchmark transfer. Between the near-clone pair PGS000078 vs PGS000789, PGS000789 is explicitly an inverse-weight reparameterization of PGS000078 with essentially identical full-model metrics/covariates, so there is no clear multi-field advantage to overturn the upstream top-ranked PGS000078.

PGS002768 is the best direct-match osteoporosis PRS in this shortlist because it targets the generic osteoporosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis) and is built with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants), with a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) in European evaluation (n=39,444). The top-ranked alternatives PGS001274/PGS001273 come from a known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-framework ("across 813 traits") with very low PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC ~0.576/0.569; R2 ~0.009/0.0069) and one is additionally a time-to-event subtype (osteoporosis without pathological fracture), which is a less clean match to the generic target. The 2024 Commun Biol scores (PGS004565/PGS004560/PGS004495/PGS004490) report only modest ORs (best ~1.33) with unknown covariates and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2, offering less interpretable evidence than PGS002768 while not clearly exceeding it on effect size.

PGS001312 is the strongest direct-match psoriasis PRS in this shortlist because it provides clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6916; PGS-only R2=0.0523) on a European validation record with only basic covariates, and it is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS) rather than EUR-only. The closest runner-up is PGS001313 from the same snpnet/UKB framework family, but it targets a time-to-event endpoint (TTE psoriasis) and has weaker PRS-only metrics (AUROC=0.6729; R2=0.0497). Other candidates (PGS002083/PGS001871) report only partial correlation (not directly comparable to AUROC/R2 here), and PGS002293 is an incident/lifestyle-packaged analysis with GW-significant SNPs rather than a general-purpose PRS; PGS002661/PGS002344 report only small incremental R2 in full models, offering less direct PRS discrimination evidence.

PGS000903 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused candidate: it targets Parkinson’s disease with matching EFO/phenotyping, is derived from the large Lancet Neurology PD GWAS meta-analysis study family, uses a more polygenic C+T construction (1805 variants) than its sibling PGS000902 (90 variants), and shows stronger reported discrimination/effect evidence in the selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.692 and OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25). The main runner-up is PGS000902 from the same publication with identical covariates and validation size, but it is a much sparser genome-wide-significant score and has weaker AUROC (0.651) with no compensating effect-size metrics. Other candidates either rely on heavier clinical covariate packaging (PGS001774 includes family history and multiple risk factors), incorporate non-PRS genetic burden terms (PGS000750 includes singleton LoF count and family history), or provide weaker/less comparable performance reporting despite large samples (PGS003763 HR only).

All candidates are direct matches for thyroid carcinoma with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so selection hinges on study design/covariate cleanliness and avoiding covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. PGS000632 (Cancer PRSweb) uses only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs) and has a larger validation sample (n=4,270) than the other PRSweb siblings, with similar effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.568). The strongest runner-up is PGS000208, which shows a much higher AUROC (0.751) but that is a full-model AUROC and is explicitly augmented with family history, making it less comparable to standalone PRS performance and more likely inflated. Given the domain guidance to heavily discount family-history-boosted full-model AUROC, PGS000632 is the safer best-supported direct PRS candidate.

PGS001137 is the cleanest direct match to the target endpoint (“Retinal detachment” across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported) and it reports explicit PRS-only performance (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.573 and PGS R2(no covariates)=0.00663), which is interpretable and remains below the local h2_obs ceiling (~0.0042) in the expected small-signal range. Against the strongest runner-up PGS002040 (same general phenotype but broader/less specific label “detachments and defects” and only a partial-correlation metric), PGS001137 provides more directly comparable PRS-only metrics and slightly stronger signal than the sibling PGS001833 (partial-r 0.0218) and the related-but-time-to-event/breaks-packaged PGS000990 (lower PRS-only AUROC 0.542 and R2 0.00213).

All three candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping all match carcinoma in situ of skin), ancestry (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), cohorts (MGI), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and validation size (n=5,500), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2—so we should not treat full-model AUROC as a PRS-comparable metric. In this same-study, same-endpoint setting, the best available tie-break is within-family empirical performance/effect-size evidence: PGS000471 has the highest reported AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557 for PGS000470 and 0.524 for PGS000469), the highest pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154 vs 0.00141), and stronger effect sizes (OR per SD 1.401; top-1% OR 3.77) than the strongest runner-up PGS000470 (OR 1.308; top-1% OR 2.45). PGS000469 underperforms on these same-context metrics despite its genome-wide variant count, so PGS000471 is the best-supported direct match.

PGS005217 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused PAD score: it targets peripheral artery disease with an incident PAD endpoint, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (~1.3M), and is evaluated broadly across multiple ancestries with a large validation sample (n=304,294). It also reports a strong PRS effect size (HR per SD 1.66), supporting meaningful discrimination even though PRS-only AUC/R2 are not provided (the reported C-index 0.731 is full-model and not directly comparable). The main runner-up among exact-label matches is PGS002055 (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified), but it comes from a UKB portability framework paper with only a weak partial correlation (partial-r 0.0175) and less endpoint specificity; PGS001843 is similar but weaker (partial-r 0.0151). PGS005158 is PAD but restricted to type 2 diabetes and uses only 19 GWAS-significant SNPs with a much smaller effect (HR 1.13) and heavy clinical covariate packaging, making it less suitable as a general peripheral vascular disease PRS.

PGS005219 is the strongest direct-match, disease-focused obstructive sleep apnea score in the shortlist: it targets the dominant clinical subtype (OSA) with coherent phenotyping, uses a genome-wide shrinkage/aggregation-style construction (PRS-CSs weighted summation) with ~983k variants, and is developed/validated in a multi-cohort setting (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry evaluation. Versus the closest runner-up PGS005220 (same study family, same validation context), PGS005219 shows materially stronger PRS effect-size evidence (OR 1.98 vs 1.53), while both only report full-model AUROC (0.79) that is not PRS-comparable and both include BMI among covariates. The older MVP GWAS-hits scores (PGS003857/PGS003858) are much sparser (18/6 variants) and the ExPRSweb ‘sleep apnea’ framework scores (PGS003210/PGS003211/PGS003213) have weak discrimination (AUROC ~0.52) and are less disease-focused.

All three candidates are broadly aligned to pulmonary fibrosis, but PGS001791 is the best-supported direct-match for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in a way that is most likely to transfer: it is a genome-wide shrinkage PRS (PRS-CS-auto; 910,439 variants) developed in a large multi-biobank/global framework and evaluated in a very large European sample (n=347,350) with a clean PRS-comparable metric reported (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out / PGS-only R2=0.005929), which is plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0039) and indicates nontrivial PRS signal. The strongest runner-up, PGS001030, has higher reported PGS-only R2 (0.0142) but comes from the known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“813 traits”) with only 51 variants, a setting that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external generalization; its broader ‘pulmonary fibrosis’ endpoint is also less specific than IPF. PGS004695 is disease-aligned but is a 23-SNP GWS score embedded in an exposure-focused incident-IPF study and provides no PRS-only AUC/R2 (only an HR high-vs-low quintile), making it less directly comparable and less structurally robust than PGS001791.

All top four candidates (PGS000136/133/134/135) are near-clones from the same schizophrenia-focused paper with identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/efo/phenotyping all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same basic covariates, and EUR-only evaluation—so the main differentiators are the within-family performance/effect-size signals and structural variant count. PGS000136 has the strongest available effect-size evidence (OR per SD ~1.7, vs 1.691 for PGS000133 and notably lower 1.483 for PGS000134) and also a higher full-model AUROC (0.64) than the other large-validation siblings (0.60), while maintaining a high variant count (833k). Although PGS000135 shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.74), it lacks effect-size reporting and is supported by a much smaller validation sample (n=9,569), making that AUROC more likely to be unstable/outlier within this near-clone set. PGS002785 is not a direct endpoint match because phenotyping_reported is cognitive function rather than schizophrenia diagnosis, so it is deprioritized despite having an R2-like metric.

All candidates are direct matches for prostate cancer with identical phenotype fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), same publication family, same training cohort (UKB), same training N (9,671), same evaluation context (EUR with some SAS), and similarly clean covariate reporting (covariates=0). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 available for any candidate, the best differentiators are within-family performance and structural advantages. PGS004155 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.7049 vs 0.7003 for the strongest runner-up PGS004139) and the strongest effect size (OR per SD 2.166 vs 2.112), and it uses an ensemble/multi-PRS approach with the largest variant count (~1.14M), which is a positive structural signal when endpoints and covariates are otherwise near-clones. The AUROC differences are modest, but the consistent edge in both AUROC and OR over the closest single-method alternatives supports selecting PGS004155.

All candidates are direct matches to type 2 diabetes, but PGS002308 has the strongest overall evidence package for external transfer: it is explicitly a trans-ancestry PRS-CSx score with broad multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/GME), supporting robustness beyond a single EUR-only setting. Its reported per-SD effect size is strong (OR=1.96) and it uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, site), avoiding the heavier BMI-adjusted packaging seen in PGS005246. The main runner-up is PGS005246 (also PRS-CSx) with similar full-model AUROC and OR, but it is EUR-only evaluation and includes BMI in covariates, making its reported discrimination less comparable and potentially more covariate-driven. The UKBB five-biobank method-benchmark siblings (PGS004152/4068/4052/4039) have much lower reported AUROC/OR in their selected records and are EUR-GWAS-only, so they do not clearly beat the trans-ancestry, multi-ancestry-validated PGS002308 despite lacking PRS-only AUC/R2 fields across the shortlist.

PGS001280 is the best direct match to the target trait (pulmonary embolism) in both trait_efo and phenotyping_reported (TTE PE) without bundling DVT, whereas the closest runner-up by metrics (PGS001277) is a composite PE +/- DVT endpoint (trait_efo includes DVT), reducing endpoint fidelity. Among the PE-focused options, PGS001280 also provides clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.60765; PGS-only R2=0.01403) with basic covariates and these values are plausible under the PE heritability ceiling, while the newer ICD10 I26 models (PGS004530/PGS004460) lack comparable PRS-only performance metrics and appear to be risk-factor integration variants with unknown covariates, and the EAS-only PRSice score (PGS003861) reports only a full-model AUROC (0.765) with unknown covariates, making it non-comparable as a standalone PRS. Given the shortlist and the weak-prior ranking order, PGS001280 remains the most supported direct-match candidate.

All candidates map to ulcerative colitis, but PGS004253 is the only clearly disease-focused UC PRS in this shortlist (Nat Commun; UC-specific application) using a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2-auto; 744,575 variants) and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.84, 95% CI 1.76–1.93), which is a strong predictor of real-world PRS discrimination. The main runner-up is PGS001306, which has clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 (PGS-only AUROC=0.630, R2=0.020) but comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse-framework paper (813 traits) with only 179 variants—an archetype that often generalizes worse externally despite tidy metrics. PGS001307 is time-to-event (endpoint mismatch risk) and the portability-paper scores (PGS001855/PGS002066) lack PRS-only metrics here and show weaker/less informative performance signals (e.g., PGS002066 full-model AUROC=0.57; OR=1.11). Thus, PGS004253 has the best overall endpoint-faithful, method/coverage, and effect-size evidence versus the strongest framework competitor.

PGS002075 is the top-ranked candidate and is a direct match to the target (trait_efo=urolithiasis; phenotyping_reported/trait_reported=Urinary calculus). Within the same publication family and endpoint as the strongest runner-up (PGS001864), it shows better PRS signal via higher partial correlation (0.0385 vs 0.0323) while sharing the same training cohort (UKB), training size, covariates, and multi-ancestry evaluation structure—making the metric comparison valid. The alternatives are less compelling: PGS001250 is a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score with a time-to-event endpoint and only modest PRS-only AUROC/R2, and PGS004563/PGS004493 are risk-factor integration study scores with unknown covariates and only modest per-SD ORs, providing weaker comparable performance evidence.

PGS004163 is the strongest direct-match within the main coherent sibling cluster (same publication family, same seropositive RA endpoint, same ancestry context, and covariates=0), and it has the best within-cluster performance/effect-size evidence (highest full-model AUROC 0.7469 and highest OR per SD 2.46) compared with the closest runner-up PGS004049 (AUROC 0.7283, OR 2.37). The alternative high C-index model PGS004873 is less endpoint-aligned for a generic RA target (incident-only RA) and is a framework-style absolute-incidence paper with different covariates (PCs 1–10) and much smaller validation (n=7,018), making its high C-index less comparable/supportive for standalone RA PRS selection than the well-supported five-biobank evaluation family represented by PGS004163.

All candidates are direct phenotype matches (trait_reported/efo/phenotyping_reported all ‘Squamous cell carcinoma’) and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we should not treat full-model AUROC as a PRS-comparable differentiator. Within the tight Cancer PRSweb sibling cluster (PGS000461/463/465/467/464) with essentially identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and EUR-only context, PGS000461 has the strongest overall discrimination evidence (highest full-model AUROC 0.599 and highest per-SD OR 1.491) versus the closest runner-up PGS000465 (AUROC 0.589, OR 1.457). PGS000731 has slightly higher AUROC (0.605) and larger validation N but has unknown covariates and lacks training/sample details, making its AUROC less interpretable/comparable; thus it does not clearly beat the best-supported PRSweb sibling. Upstream ranking prior also favors PGS000461.

All candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (same trait_efo), and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we should not over-weight full-model AUROC. Within the strongest near-clone family (Cancer PRSweb UKB-developed scores with identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry and same training N=12,992), PGS000613 (P+T, 15 variants) has consistently better within-family performance than the top-ranked sibling PGS000611 (GWAS hits, 13 variants): higher full-model AUROC (0.571 vs 0.567), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0125 vs 0.0114), and stronger top-1% vs rest OR (2.91 vs 2.66) with the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs). Other candidates either come from the smaller MGI-developed set (PGS000610/612/616) with weaker or much worse metrics (lassosum AUROC 0.538), or have less complete/less comparable metadata despite large evaluation (PGS000723, PGS004687). Thus PGS000613 has the clearest multi-field advantage over the closest runner-up (PGS000611) in the most comparable context.

PGS000922 is the best direct match to the target trait (trait_efo=sarcoidosis; phenotyping_reported=Sarcoidosis) and provides clean PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64282; PGS-only R2=0.01741) under basic covariates, with multi-ancestry evaluation listed. The strongest runner-up is PGS000923, which has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 but is explicitly a time-to-event endpoint (phenotyping_reported=TTE sarcoidosis; trait_reported includes time-to-event), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic sarcoidosis target. The other two candidates (PGS001872, PGS002084) are mapped to skin sarcoidosis in trait_efo and only report partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R2), making them less directly comparable and less endpoint-faithful despite larger variant counts.

PGS003381 is the strongest direct-match for the target concept (uterine cancer) because it targets the clinically dominant subtype (uterine endometrial carcinoma / endometrial carcinoma) and uses a genome-wide PRS (lassosum; 529,365 variants) with only basic covariates (age + 20 PCs), avoiding heavy clinical packaging. Against the strongest runner-up PGS001795 (exact uterine cancer label), PGS001795 comes from a global-biobank framework paper and its only PRS-comparable metric is a very small covariates-regressed-out R2=0.001948 (below the local h2_liability ceiling 0.0116), suggesting weak standalone PRS signal despite huge variant count; its AUROC=0.66 is full-model and not PRS-only. PGS003381 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2, but its endpoint fidelity plus genome-wide construction and clean covariates make it more likely to transfer well than the framework-derived, low-R2 alternative; the older sparse GWAS-hits uterus scores (PGS000541/PGS000542) and very small-sample corpus uteri score (PGS003740) are structurally weaker.

PGS001536 is the only candidate with coherent vitiligo endpoint metadata (trait_efo=Vitiligo; phenotyping_reported=TTE vitiligo) and clean PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193; PGS-only R2=0.01621), with basic covariates and a heritability-sane R2 (well below h2_obs~0.17). The main runner-up by label (PGS000738) has a clear phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported=Red hair) and only a pseudo R2/full-model-style metric with unknown covariates, making it non-comparable and likely mis-mapped. PGS000760 is also endpoint-mismatched (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients) despite the vitiligo label, so it is not a direct-match vitiligo PRS for general use.

All candidates are direct matches to type 1 diabetes mellitus by trait_efo, but PGS004162 has the strongest overall evidence package among the top-ranked options: it is a genome-wide, multi-PRS/ensemble-style score (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; 62,645 variants) with no non-genetic covariates (covariates=0), and it reports strong PRS-relevant effect sizes (OR per SD 2.89) plus solid discrimination (full-model AUROC ~0.77) in a large evaluation (n=90,274; EUR with some SAS). The strongest runner-up is PGS000024 (ranked #1), which shows a very high AUROC (0.921) but only as a full-model metric with unknown covariates and a GWAS-hits/interaction model (85 variants), making that AUROC likely less comparable to standalone PRS performance. Compared with its near-clone sibling PGS004078 from the same study family and evaluation setting, PGS004162 is consistently better (higher AUROC, higher R2, higher OR), so it is the best-supported choice within that coherent family.
